description: issue #688 (terminal slice, review round 1): the ACTIVE half of `spec/interaction-events.md:43-46` -- `when`, `every`, `on_key`, and `on_click` are profile block-heads, and they are reserved WITHIN the Interaction & Events profile. Redefining any of the four with `define` raises `ol-reserved-word`, and all four are asserted in one program so a fix that reserved only the name a single fixture happened to pick cannot pass. `params.namespace` is `reserved` -- the RESERVED-WORD branch of the rule -- which is what distinguishes these four from the profile's ordinary primitives: the sibling `redefine-wait-reserved` pins `wait` at `namespace: "primitive"` because `wait` is a primitive name and not a reserved block-head. Before this fixture the corpus proved the primitive branch only, so the four block-heads' reservation -- a normative MUST -- rested on unit tests alone and no other implementation was bound by it (the same gap class the Sprites terminal slice #679 found for its own `ol-reserved-word` rule). Its twin `block-heads-free-core-only` proves the `only within` half: the SAME source is clean Core-only. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static legality only and does not execute.

diagnostics.message: when is already a reserved, so it can't be redefined here.
every is already a reserved, so it can't be redefined here.
